title: Expansion of a free Fermi gas released from an isotropic trapping potential
authors: J M Luck, P L Krapivsky
abstract: We consider a system of non-interacting fermions prepared in the many-body ground state of an isotropic trapping potential in any dimension, and investigate the ballistic expansion of the fermionic cloud after the potential is suddenly released. Using semi-classical techniques, we derive the full late-time profile of the expanding cloud in the regime when the fermion number is large. We thus obtain explicit expressions for power-law potentials with arbitrary exponent $a$ and in all dimensions $d$. The momentum distribution and the spatial profile of the cloud exhibit a universal edge exponent $d/a$, thus generalizing the Wigner semi-circle law and the Thomas-Fermi distribution.
summary: This paper theoretically analyzes the expansion of a free Fermi gas released from an isotropic trap. Using semi-classical methods, it derives universal power-law scaling laws for the density profile in arbitrary dimensions and for potentials with any exponent. The results generalize fundamental distributions like the Wigner semi-circle law to non-equilibrium dynamics.
main_problem: The study investigates the time evolution and late-time spatial profile of a free Fermi gas after its confining isotropic potential is suddenly removed.
main_result: The paper derives explicit, universal power-law scaling for the density profile $ho_N(r; t)$ in arbitrary dimensions $d$ and for potentials with general exponents $a$, generalizing known results like the Wigner semi-circle law.
method: Semi-classical techniques are employed to analyze the large-$N$ limit, treating the dynamics via expectation values derived from the initial many-body ground state wavefunction.
model_or_system: The system is a non-interacting Fermi gas confined by an isotropic trapping potential $V(x)$ in any dimension. The analysis covers both the exactly solvable harmonic case and general power-law potentials $V(x) \sim |x|^a$.
key_observables: Total fermion density $ho_N(r; t)$, momentum distribution, and moments $\mu_{2k}(t)$ of the expanding cloud.
important_parameters: Fermion number ($N$), dimensionality ($d$), potential exponent ($a$), and time ($t$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the semi-classical limit for large fermion numbers ($N \gg 1$) and assumes sudden release of the trapping potential.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate scaling functions $A(\xi)$ (harmonic trap) and $F(\xi)$ (square-well potential), showing how the density profile evolves away from initial equilibrium distributions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the general formalism for calculating time-dependent expectation values, solving the exactly solvable harmonic case using GUE statistics, and finally generalizing the results to arbitrary power-law potentials in the semi-classical limit.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous theoretical framework for understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in quantum many-body systems, particularly how initial confinement dictates long-time ballistic spreading, which is crucial for modeling trapped atomic gases or quantum fluids.
